note: Single source of truth for RBAC. Every permission string is 'resource:action'. apps/api/src/lib/permissions.ts loads this file and exposes hasPermission(role, permission); apps/api tests assert every (role, permission) pair against this matrix exactly (see docs/SECURITY.md for the rendered table).

separationOfDuties.note: recommendation:approve gates POST /api/v1/decisions (creating a Decision — approve/modify/reject/defer a Recommendation). It is granted to DISTRICT_OFFICER (the operational approver role) and to SUPER_ADMIN (which has every permission by definition, including break-glass override), and explicitly withheld from every other role — most importantly STATE_ADMIN, which has broad read/write but is structurally barred from being the approver of the recommendations its own state's data feeds into: whoever can edit the inputs (habitation/hazardZone/hazardEvent/relocationSite:write) must not routinely approve the output. recommendation:approveEscalated is the documented exception to that restriction, not a repeal of it: it is granted to STATE_ADMIN (and SUPER_ADMIN) but the decision route additionally requires, server-side, that the specific recommendation being decided has escalation.status === 'ESCALATED' — set only by a DISTRICT_OFFICER's (or SUPER_ADMIN's, on the district officer's behalf) explicit ESCALATE decision, itself requiring the same >=30-character justification as every other decision. A STATE_ADMIN can never act on a recommendation nobody escalated. Every decision taken this way is marked decisionLevel: 'STATE' (vs. 'DISTRICT' for everything else) in the Decision record and the audit trail, with WARNING audit severity instead of INFO, so it is always visibly distinguishable from an ordinary district-level decision — see docs/SECURITY.md's escalation section.
